page: Microsoft Azure L80as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine designed for high-throughput, low-latency I/O operations and memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Driven by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance runs on the x86_64 architecture using AMD EPYC 9V74 processors clocked at 3.7 GHz. Compute resources comprise 80 dedicated virtual CPUs across 40 physical cores with multi-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16), and advanced cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The server profile incorporates 640.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. Local ephemeral capacity includes 19,199 GB of high-speed NVMe solid-state storage directly attached to the host, providing substantial IOPS and low-latency disk access without requiring external network-attached volumes for scratch space. The system features no onboard graphics processors and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating standard Azure virtual network routing or external IP provisioning for outbound and inbound connectivity.

Benchmark results highlight strong computational and data handling metrics. Geekbench multi-core evaluations yield a score of 22,523.0, placing it in the top tier, paired with a Clang compilation score of 61,006.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 86,210.97. Single-threaded performance remains strong, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2,083.0. Uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidths reach 190.57 GB/sec and 117.51 GB/sec respectively, supporting rapid processing in data-intensive frameworks. In-memory operations show high throughput, registering 106.48 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 28,377.64 in PassMark database operations.

Hardware density offers high cost efficiency for organizations consolidating demanding disk and memory footprints into a single node. The bundled 19.19 TB NVMe array offsets the potential storage costs of attaching large external block stores. However, the local storage remains ephemeral, meaning application architectures must handle data replication and persistence elsewhere. Best-fit deployments include distributed NoSQL databases, transactional relational databases, large-scale Redis or Memcached clusters, data warehousing, and high-throughput real-time log analytics.
description: Microsoft Azure L80as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by 80 dedicated vCPUs on a 40-core AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with Hyper-V virtualization, the instance integrates AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware acceleration. It features 640.0 GB of system memory alongside an expansive 19,199 GB local NVMe SSD storage array. Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier multi-threaded processing, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core rating of 22,523.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 86,210.97, accompanied by strong database and caching metrics including over 106 million Redis SET operations per second. The dense aggregation of compute, high memory bandwidth, and high-capacity NVMe drive provides exceptional cost efficiency for read- and write-intensive systems. Microsoft Azure L80as_v4 is structured for transactional databases, NoSQL datastores, distributed search clusters, big data analytics engines, and real-time processing pipelines.
